system_overview: This specification models a distributed spanning tree construction algorithm. Starting from a designated root node, the algorithm builds a spanning tree over a network of processes connected by a given neighbor relation. Each non-root process that receives a message from a neighbor adopts that neighbor as its parent, thereby joining the tree. Processes propagate messages to their neighbors, and eventually every reachable process has a parent linking it back toward the root.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a set of processes connected by a static neighbor relation. One distinguished process serves as the root of the spanning tree. A special sentinel value represents the absence of a parent assignment. Processes communicate by sending messages (modeled as pairs of sender and receiver) through a shared message pool.
state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) a parent assignment for each process, initially set to a sentinel indicating no parent, (2) a report flag for each process indicating whether it has reported its parent assignment, and (3) a set of messages that have been sent between processes.
initial_state: All processes start with no parent assigned (set to the sentinel value). No process has reported. The message set is empty.
actions: There are three main actions: (1) Update: a non-root process that has no parent and receives a message from a neighbor adopts that neighbor as its parent. (2) Send: a process that is either the root or already has a parent sends a message to a neighbor it has not yet contacted. (3) Report (Parent): a process that has a parent and has not yet reported sets its report flag to true. At each step, a pair of processes is chosen, and if the first is a non-root with no parent that has a pending message from the second, an update occurs; otherwise one of the other actions or a stutter step is taken.
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures parent assignments respect the neighbor relation, report flags are boolean, and messages are pairs of processes. Once a process has a parent, it keeps that same parent forever (one-parent stability). A sent-message property ensures that processes without parents do not appear as senders in the message set.
liveness_properties: Under weak fairness, the algorithm terminates: eventually every non-root process has a parent that is a valid neighbor.
additional_assumptions: The neighbor relation is given as a static set of ordered pairs of processes. The algorithm assumes the network is connected from the root through the neighbor relation so that all processes are reachable.
